newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain has no plans to revalue, sell gold.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain has no plans to revalue, sell gold.

text.p: The Bank of Spain said on Friday it had no plans to revalue or to sell its gold reserves.
"We haven't sold nor changed nor do we have a plan to sell or to revalue our gold reserves," a spokesman for the central bank told Reuters.
The Bank of Spain has 16 million troy ounces of gold with a book value of $4.2 billion which has been nearly unchanged since 1991. One troy ounce is the equivalent of 31.10 grams of very pure gold.
Total Bank of Spain reserves were $65.903 billion at the end of April.
On Thursday, Germany said it planned to change Bundesbank law by summer, allowing it to raise the value of its gold and foreign exchange reserves.
The Bundesbank currently books its assets at their all-time lowest price or at the purchase price, a method which is normal under German book-keeping regulations.
A revaluation would effectively deliver Bonn a windfall profit, allowing it to retire old debt more quickly than otherwise.
The move would improve Germany's debt and deficit positions, which are key to meeting Maastricht Treaty criteria to qualify for a single European currency.
